## The whole experiment, then a selected comparison

The tutorial starts with `investigation.csv` (26 rats) and `replicates.csv` (47 cells), spanning both conditioning protocols and all three phases. `study.csv`, described below, is the selected baseline/acquisition comparison used for guided statistics.

One row is one rat, summarised by the mean of its recorded cells. Baseline and acquisition use different rats, not the same rat measured twice. All core animals received the cue followed by reward protocol. In the original paper this protocol is called paired conditioning; that name does not mean our statistical samples are paired.

| Column in study.csv | Meaning |
|---|---|
| sample_id | Animal identifier |
| group | Baseline or Acquisition |
| reversal_mV | Mean GABA reversal potential (mV) |
| resting_mV | Mean resting membrane potential (mV) |

The column names identify the biological measurements;
always give the full measurement and units in a plot caption or report. CSVs are UTF-8,
comma-separated, with a header. `NA` denotes missing. Raw files are not changed by the
interactive controls or by the made-up outlier/missingness exercises.

## Chloride data: preparation and limits

Woo et al. (2025), Dynamic changes in chloride homeostasis coordinate midbrain inhibitory
network activity during reward learning, Nature Communications, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-66838-x.
Dataset DOI: 10.5061/dryad.44j0zpcv7, **CC0** (verified in Dryad API metadata).

Dryad's public download endpoint returned HTTP 403 when preparing this course. We therefore
retrieved the publisher's Source Data workbook instead. Exact URL and checksum are in
`data/source/PROVENANCE.md`. The publisher's workbook is preserved unchanged for provenance;
the article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Our course extracts factual numerical records and cites both
sources. No article figures or text have been adapted. We have not claimed byte-identical
equality between the publisher workbook and inaccessible Dryad CSV files.

### Electrical measurements

Source sheet **Figure 1G+1H**, rows 5–13, 21–32 and 38–47, columns A:C (Paired) and F:H
(Unpaired). Only rows with numeric reversal potentials are retained. Case, whitespace and
decimal commas are standardised in the source ID key. Teaching labels Rat_01–Rat_26 are assigned consistently across tables; source labels and row numbers remain in
`cells.csv`. The Unpaired cell labels are truncated in the source, so source-row identity
is retained rather than inventing cell numbers. All recorded values are preserved.

`investigation.csv` contains **26 rats**. We average reversal and resting potentials within
animal and retain `n_cells`. Thus each rat contributes once, regardless of the number of
recorded cells. This targets the mean of each animal's sampled cells, not the entire neuronal
population. It differs from the paper's cell-level analyses and should not reproduce their
p-values exactly. Sampling and averaging can affect both effect estimates and precision.

| Column | Meaning / unit |
|---|---|
| sample_id | Standardised rat ID; nominal identifier |
| conditioning | Paired cue/reward protocol or Unpaired protocol; nominal |
| phase | Baseline, Acquisition or Plateau; ordered learning phases |
| day_label | Source section label: 1, 7 or 13; acquisition spans days 5–7 in the paper |
| reversal_mV | Within-rat mean GABA reversal potential, millivolts |
| resting_mV | Within-rat mean resting membrane potential, millivolts |
| n_cells | Number of recorded cells contributing to each rat's mean; count |

Paired protocol: 7 baseline, 6 acquisition and 5 plateau rats. Unpaired protocol: 3 baseline,
3 acquisition and 2 plateau rats. The animal IDs are distinct across these groups. The word
Paired describes cue–reward timing; it does **not** make the animal groups paired samples.
Unique IDs do not rule out all other clustering, such as shared litters or cages.

`study.csv` keeps only Paired-protocol baseline and acquisition animals, **13 rats** in total.
`group` identifies the learning phase. The `reversal_mV` and `resting_mV` columns retain the animal-mean voltages described above. There are no missing
values in this core table. Negative voltages are ordinary measurements; “larger” here means
less negative, not a larger absolute magnitude. An electrical change alone does not identify
which transporter caused it.

### NKCC1 protein puzzle

Source sheet **Figure S1N**, rows 26–33: day-1 IDs and values in C:D; day-7 in F:G.
`nkcc1.csv` retains all 16 animals, the NKCC1/GAPDH band-intensity ratio, day and source row.
Batch labels February/March follow the raw image headers at rows 3 and 12: summary rows
26–29 map to February records, 30–33 to March. Each batch has four rats per day.
Ratios are preserved at source precision and are dimensionless relative band intensities.
They are not direct chloride concentration or transport-rate measurements.

This is a **descriptive extension** about assay batches, not a definitive pooled test.
The source's matching/blocking is insufficiently documented here for beginner inference.
Row alignment must not be promoted into a biological pairing assumption. Do not join this
separate experiment to electrophysiology by row order or assume all animals overlap.


## Reproducibility

The raw workbook, its SHA-256 checksum and exact download URL are preserved in `data/source/`
in the branch checkout (excluded from the small student ZIP). `scripts/prepare_data.py`
rebuilds the teaching tables; `scripts/validate_data.py` independently reconciles records,
group counts and selected transformations. No outcomes were changed to manufacture a result.

[Dataset](https://datadryad.org/dataset/doi:10.5061/dryad.44j0zpcv7) · [Study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66838-x)

## Source discrepancy retained for review

The publisher workbook contains 10 Paired-protocol plateau cells, whereas the paper Figure 1G caption reports 9. We retain all 10 recorded cells across 5 rats (47 cells overall across both protocols). No undocumented exclusion is inferred. This affects the optional plateau comparison, not the baseline/acquisition core. Treat that extension as an exploratory analysis of the supplied workbook, pending clarification of the published cell count.

## Measurement-level table for the day-1 replication investigation

`replicates.csv` contains 47 measurement rows from 26 distinct rats.
It contains the same 47 records as cells.csv, adding record_number as a sequential within-animal row index. That index is not a new source cell identity or a time point. Existing source labels, row numbers, phases, protocols and voltages are retained. The previously documented plateau count discrepancy remains explicit.

The reveal plot uses the first four Paired-protocol acquisition rats in source order only, keeping condition fixed and the plot readable. The count exercises use the full table, then return to the original comparison.
The copy-slider demonstration duplicates the original animal-level Baseline observations in memory. It labels the resulting independence-based standard error as naive; no new biological evidence is created and no data files are changed.

## Readable animal IDs and matched voltages

All electrophysiology tables now use `Rat_01`–`Rat_26`, assigned by first appearance in the source extraction. These labels encode no condition, rank or response. `animal_id_key.csv` maps each label back to the normalized original animal ID; the cell table also retains the verbatim source label and row. Measurements and membership are unchanged.

The two voltages occur on the same identified cell row in source sheet `Figure 1G+1H`. Each animal's reversal and resting means use those same cells, so they can be shown together in an animal-level scatterplot. Baseline and acquisition are different animals: this within-row matching does not justify a paired cross-phase test.

The tutorial begins with all 26 rats and 47 cells, including both protocols and all three phases. It then selects the 13-rat baseline/acquisition example explicitly. The replication exercises are integrated into sections 2, 3 and 7.
